level_1: Elicits and presents a history and performs a vascular examination relevant to the patient’s presenting complaint
level_2: Orders and interprets diagnostic testing; establishes differential diagnosis
level_3: Synthesizes patient data, including diagnostic imaging, to arrive at an organized hierarchical differential diagnosis for basic disease processes, to include primary and secondary treatment options
level_4: Synthesizes patient data, including diagnostic imaging, to arrive at an organized hierarchical differential diagnosis for complex disease processes with advanced comorbidities, to include primary and secondary treatment options
level_5: Synthesizes patient data, including diagnostic imaging, to arrive at an organized hierarchical differential diagnosis for rare disease processes and variants of complex disease processes

level_1: Describes risk factors for vascular disease
level_2: Identifies therapies for risk factor modification
level_3: Recognizes endpoints, contraindications, and complications of medical therapy
level_4: Formulates a comprehensive plan of medical management for patients with vascular disease, including risk factor modification
level_5: Proposes novel medical treatment algorithms based on new literature

level_1: Manages basic peri- operative problems (e.g., fever, pain)
level_2: Manages common peri- operative problems (e.g., post-operative myocardial infraction), including ordering and interpretation of supplemental tests when needed
level_3: Recognizes and manages complex peri-operative problems, including vascular complications, critical care, and palliative care
level_4: Leads team and provides supervision in the evaluation and management of complex peri-operative problems, including vascular complications, critical care, and palliative care
level_5: Works with the interdisciplinary care team to develop new pathways to prevent peri-operative vascular complications

subcompetencies.name: Longitudinal Care (e.g., Outpatient Management, Screening, Surveillance)

level_1: Describes and recognizes expected longitudinal care, including outpatient management, screening, and surveillance for patients with basic vascular disease
level_2: Describes the expected longitudinal care for patients with complex vascular disease
level_3: Recognizes the impact of disease progression and complications on the longitudinal care plan
level_4: Independently alters longitudinal care based on disease progression, complications, or patient-specific issues
level_5: Innovates new aspects of longitudinal care for patients with vascular disease by considering the most updated evidence-based guidelines

level_1: Identifies and orders the tests for standard pre- operative optimization
For intermediate procedures, ensures necessary imaging, instrumentation, equipment, devices, and medications are available; positions, prepares, and drapes patient appropriately
level_2: Prepares patient for surgery, including pre- operative orders and diagnostic tests
Proposes alternative surgical plan due to patient factors or disease progression identified in pre- operative work-up
level_3: Interprets clinical data to identify opportunities for pre-operative optimization
For advanced procedures, ensures necessary imaging, instrumentation, equipment, devices, and medications are available; positions, prepares, and drapes patient appropriately
level_4: For basic procedures, ensures necessary imaging, instrumentation, equipment, devices, and medications are available; positions, prepares, and drapes patient appropriately
Proposes novel therapies to address a patient that is not a candidate for standard care
level_5: Recognizes when procedural plan must change due to patient factors or disease progression identified in pre-operative work-up
Develops protocols to improve the procedural preparation process

level_1: Demonstrates basic surgical skills and performs basic bedside procedures
Proficiently handles instruments and equipment, uses assistants, guides the conduct of the operation, and makes independent intra- operative decisions; anticipates when assistance is needed
level_2: Demonstrates respect for tissue, and is developing skill in instrument handling
Performs advanced vascular procedures, including troubleshooting and managing complications with limited supervision
level_3: Performs basic vascular procedures with limited supervision
Handles instruments and equipment independently without supervision, guides the conduct of the operation, and makes intra-operative decisions
level_4: Handles vascular instruments with increasing efficiency of motion during procedures
Competently teaches intermediate vascular procedures
level_5: Performs basic vascular procedures independently and intermediate vascular procedures with limited supervision

level_1: Uses ultrasound to demonstrate anatomy for vascular access
Troubleshoots and manages basic procedural challenges
level_2: Recognizes the importance of maintaining wire position during wire and catheter exchanges
Performs advanced endovascular procedures with appropriate wire and catheter skills
level_3: Uses ultrasound to safely obtain percutaneous arterial and/or venous access in most patients
Identifies when to select an alternative access site, wire and catheter technique, or approach to troubleshoot complex procedural challenges
level_4: Selects wires and catheters and demonstrates basic wire handling techniques and performs most catheter exchanges without losing wire position
Suggests novel endovascular therapies for most complex cases, including troubleshooting and managing endovascular complications
level_5: Performs basic and intermediate procedures

subcompetencies.name: Vascular Imaging (e.g., Computed Tomography [CT], Magnetic Resonance [MR], Angiography, Ultrasonography)

level_1: Identifies the various types of imaging modalities
Uses imaging findings to support differential diagnosis, pre-operative plan, and intra-operative decision making for advanced vascular procedures
level_2: Uses imaging findings to support differential diagnosis and pre- operative plan for basic vascular procedures
Independently uses multidimensional imaging (e.g., 3-D computed tomography angiography [CTA]) and identifies abnormal findings
level_3: Describes patient factors that influence the imaging modality
Implements innovative imaging technology to enhance the care of the patient
level_4: Uses imaging findings to support differential diagnosis and pre- operative plan for intermediate vascular procedures
Teaches imaging interpretation of multiple modalities
level_5: Uses complementary information from varying imaging studies

level_1: Identifies the need for intervention over medical management
level_2: Synthesizes clinical data to choose an open surgical procedure versus endovascular intervention
level_3: Develops a specific operative plan for the current clinical situation, understanding alternative surgical options
level_4: Adapts management plan for changing clinical situation
level_5: Develops new guidelines or innovative applications

level_1: Identifies the need for intervention over medical management
level_2: Synthesizes clinical data to choose an endovascular intervention versus open surgical procedure
level_3: Develops a specific endovascular plan for the current clinical situation, understanding device instructions for use and limitations
level_4: Adapts management plan for changing clinical situation and understands alternative or off label endovascular options
level_5: Develops new guidelines or innovative applications

subcompetencies.name: Procedural Understanding, including Anatomy (Open Surgical Procedures)

level_1: Identifies the types of procedures for a patient’s pathology
Describes or develops an innovative approach in peer-reviewed literature
level_2: Identifies appropriate procedure
level_3: Describes procedural sequence and equipment needs, and understands critical decision points of basic procedures
level_4: Describes procedural sequence and equipment needs, and understands critical decision points of intermediate procedures
level_5: Describes procedural sequence and equipment needs, and understands critical decision points of advanced procedures

level_1: Identifies the types of procedures for a patient’s pathology
level_2: Describes procedural sequence and understands critical decision points of basic procedures
level_3: Describes procedural sequence and equipment needs, and understands critical decision points of intermediate procedures
level_4: Describes procedural sequence and equipment needs, and understands critical decision points of advanced procedures
level_5: Describes or develops an innovative approach in peer-reviewed literature

level_1: Describes potential crises during vascular procedures
level_2: Describes intra-operative findings associated with a crisis
level_3: Describes appropriate response to a crisis, including imaging and possible interventions
level_4: Anticipates patient- specific risk for crisis and describes appropriate treatment algorithm and potential outcomes, including conversion to an alternate procedure
level_5: Describes, develops, or publishes an innovative approach or otherwise impacts patient care, delivery, or quality

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
level_3: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Discloses patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
level_4: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_5: Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality metrics and quality improvement methodologies
level_2: Describes local quality improvement initiatives (e.g., infection rate, smoking cessation)
level_3: Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
level_4: Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_5: Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties
level_3: Coordinates multidisciplinary care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional team members
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems, including outpatient settings
level_4: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_5: Coordinates multidisciplinary care of patients in complex clinical situations, including those with barriers to access, effectively using the roles of the interprofessional team members
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
level_2: Identifies specific population and community health needs for their local population
level_3: Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
level_4: Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_5: Leads innovations, publishes peer-reviewed paper, or advocates for populations and communities with specific health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system (e.g., hospital, skilled nursing facility, finance, personnel, technology)
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Demonstrates core administrative knowledge needed for transition to practice
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems (e.g., government, private, public, uninsured care) and practice models
Engages with patients in shared decision making, informed by each patient’s payment models
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient and effective patient care and transitions of care
level_3: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and understands how this impacts patient care
Demonstrates use of information technology required for medical practice
Participates in local, regional, or national health policy advocacy activities
level_4: Delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment model (e.g., insurance type)
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transitions of care
Proposes changes to patient care or billing practices to improve compliance and reimbursement
level_5: Identifies the need for timely documentation to support billing
Advocates for patient care needs (e.g., community resources, patient assistance resources) with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment model

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of the mechanisms of radiation injury and the ALARA (“as low as reasonably achievable”) concept
Uses radiation protection devices, including shielding, as appropriate, with guidance
Creates, implements, and assesses radiation safety initiatives at the institutional level
level_2: Wears lead apron and dosimeter at all times
Accesses resources to determine exam-specific radiation dose information
Participates in radiation safety education and research
level_3: Applies principles of
Independently uses radiation protection devices, including shielding, as appropriate
level_4: ALARA in daily practice
Communicates the relative risk and benefits of exam-specific radiation exposure to patients and practitioners
level_5: Uses fluoroscopy techniques that decrease exposure, with guidance
Counsels colleagues and allied health staff regarding radiation exposure

level_1: Demonstrates effective access and use of available evidence to guide routine patient care
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Identifies and applies the best available evidence and integrates data to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence, even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence, to guide care tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients, and/or participates in the development of peer- reviewed literature or guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Establishes goals for personal and professional development

level_4: Revises learning plan based on performance data
level_5: Coaches others in the design and implementation of learning plans

level_1: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations and takes responsibility for own lapses

level_4: Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others
level_5: Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying informed consent, surrogate decision making, advance directives, confidentiality, error disclosure, stewardship of limited resources, and related topics

level_3: Applies ethical principles to complex situations
level_4: Resolves ethical dilemmas using appropriate resources (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)

level_1: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations

level_1: With assistance, recognizes status of personal and professional well-being

level_1: Communicates with patients and their families in an understandable and respectful manner

level_1: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
